name: Constrained container
description: Column-count caps for a section that should be narrower than the full 12: 10, 8 or 6 columns' worth of width, computed from the 1440 grid rather than typed as a pixel value. These are modifiers, not containers — each is combined with .container, which supplies the centring and the side margins, and only overrides the cap. This is the right answer to 'I need this section narrower': it keeps the measurement on the grid instead of inventing a max-width, which is the failure Will flagged in Milo's own container code.

breakpointBehavior.behavior: No effect — the cap is wider than the viewport, so the container behaves as full width.
No effect in practice at tablet widths.

tokens.note: The gutter is part of the width maths, so a gutter change moves these caps with it.

classes.name: container-10

decisions.question: The caps are computed from a hard-coded 1440 basis rather than from --s2a-grid-max-width. Should they follow the standard container up to 1920 in HD?
decisions.evidence: If the standard container rises to 1920 at XL but container-8 stays pinned to a 1440 basis, a 'two-thirds width' section quietly becomes a smaller share of the page in HD. Deliberate or not, it should be stated.

decisions.question: Will's hosted demo documents these under a heading reading 'Desktop Constraint Variations (1024px+)', but they carry no media query at all in either stylesheet.
decisions.evidence: Stale heading on acom-prototypes.vercel.app/s2a-grids/col-system.html, and 1024 is the same wrong number that caused the sectional-token reflow bug. Worth correcting on the page so nobody implements to it.

decisions.question: Should .container-6 used on its own be an error? Alone it sets only a cap — no centring, no side margins — so a section that forgets .container silently sits flush left.
decisions.evidence: The stylesheet comment calls them 'Desktop Container Modifiers' but nothing enforces the pairing. Caught while building the Storybook demo, which rendered .container-6 alone and produced a left-aligned box.
